primitives.name: Wordalisation Pipeline
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — the **wordalisation** pipeline (interpretable additive model → mean-centered feature contributions → synthesized factual text → LLM few-shot rewriting) is directly portable to GSE's public pick-explanation lane: turn engine-pick feature contributions into engaging, faithful pick narratives for X posts, feed articles, and newsletters.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'β_j': 'feature coefficient (dimensionless)', 'x̃_j': 'normalized feature value (dimensionless)', 'φ_i': 'SHAP value contribution (log-odds)', 'T': 'template sentence set (categorical)'}
primitives.assumptions: Model is additive or SHAP-compatible; feature contributions are meaningful; LLM prompt fidelity preserves semantic integrity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When |φ_i| < 0.1 log-odds, contribution is deemed negligible.

layer2.mapping: Feature contributions (β_j·x̃_j or φ_i) are mapped to narrative templates T via LLM prompting, preserving interpretability while enhancing engagement.
layer2.telemetry: Engagement score (0–5) averaged over 10 runs; accuracy judged by LLM against ground truth.

primitives.name: Percentile Edge Categorization
primitives.verbatim_quote: xG → percentile categories: "slim chance" (<25th pct, xG < 0.028), "low chance" (<50th, <0.056), "decent chance" (<75th, <0.096), "high-quality chance" (<90th, <0.3), "excellent chance" (>90th, >0.3).
primitives.latex: \text{Edge Category}(p) = \begin{cases} \text{slim} & p < 0.25 \\ \text{low} & 0.25 \leq p < 0.5 \\ \text{decent} & 0.5 \leq p < 0.75 \\ \text{high-quality} & 0.75 \leq p < 0.9 \\ \text{excellent} & p \geq 0.9 \end{cases}
primitives.assumptions: Engine probabilities are well-calibrated; percentile bins reflect historical distribution of outcomes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Below 0.25 or above 0.9, edge is considered extreme.

layer2.mapping: Probability-based edge categories are derived from engine output and used to inform narrative framing in the wordalisation process.
layer2.telemetry: Distribution of edge categories across engine picks; consistency with historical performance.

primitives.name: Feature Contribution Ranking
primitives.verbatim_quote: Contributions ranked by magnitude; only |contribution| > 0.1 log-odds included (threshold "somewhat arbitrary" — ±0.1 → small log-odds shifts).
primitives.assumptions: Log-odds scale is appropriate for ranking; threshold is empirically determined.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Features with |φ_i| ≤ 0.1 are excluded from narrative synthesis.

layer2.mapping: Only significant contributions (|φ_i| > 0.1) are selected for inclusion in the narrative, ensuring relevance and clarity.
layer2.telemetry: Number of features included per pick; average magnitude of selected features.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper is that machine learning model outputs can be transformed into natural language narratives through a structured pipeline. The wordalisation process begins with an interpretable additive model, where each feature contributes additively to the outcome. These contributions are mean-centered to remove bias and then converted into synthetic factual text. This text is subsequently rewritten by an LLM using a few-shot prompt protocol. The pipeline is designed to balance engagement and accuracy, with full wordalisation achieving both. In GSI, this translates to Bayesian updating of beliefs based on engine predictions and their feature contributions, using calibrated percentiles to categorize edge strength. In GSE, the same mechanism enables dynamic content generation for public consumption, where feature rankings determine narrative focus. The mathematical structure underpins the isomorphism between model interpretation and narrative synthesis, with the LLM serving as a semantic bridge.
